definitions.explanation: A written or printed symbol representing a sound or concept in a language.

examples.japanese: この{文字|もじ}は{何|なん}と{読|よ}みますか。
examples.english: How do you read this character?

examples.japanese: {日本語|にほんご}には{三|みっ}つの{文字|もじ}{体系|たいけい}がある。
examples.notes: ひらがな, カタカナ, 漢字

examples.japanese: {文字|もじ}を{大|おお}きく{書|か}いてください。

notes:
{文字|もじ} is the general term for any written character or letter, regardless of writing system.

READINGS:
- もじ: the standard reading
- もんじ: a less common variant reading (same meaning)

JAPANESE WRITING SYSTEMS:
- {漢字|かんじ}: kanji (Chinese characters)
- ひらがな: hiragana
- カタカナ: katakana
- アルファベット: alphabet (Latin letters)
- {数字|すうじ}: numerals

COMMON COMPOUNDS:
- {文字|もじ}{通|どお}り: literally
- {文字|もじ}{化|か}け: garbled text (encoding errors)
- {絵|え}{文字|もじ}: emoji, pictograph
- {文字|もじ}{数|すう}: character count
- {大文字|おおもじ}: uppercase letter
- {小文字|こもじ}: lowercase letter

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {文字|もじ}を{書|か}く: to write characters
- {文字|もじ}を{読|よ}む: to read characters
- {文字|もじ}が{小|ちい}さい: the characters are small
